questions.question: A shopkeeper gives a discount of 19% on marked price of article A and selling price of article B is 11(1/9)% more than selling price at article A. If shopkeeper made 20% profit on article B and selling price of article A was Rs. 840 more than cost price of article B, then find the cost price of article A. Shopkeeper sold article A at profit of 25%?
questions.explanation: Lets MP of article A = 100x Rs. Selling price of article A = 100x × (100−19)/100 = 81x Rs. Selling price of article B = 81x × 10/9 = 90x Rs. Cost price of article B = 90x/120 × 100 = 75x. Cost price of article A = 81x/125 × 100 = 64.8x Rs. Given, 81x – 75x = 840 -> 6x = 840 -> x = 140 Rs. Cost price of article A = 64.8 × 140 = 9072 Rs.

questions.question: A shopkeeper sold an article at a 10% discount at mark price. He found that he earns a profit of 16(2/3)% but instead of calculating profit on cost price he calculates it on the sum of cost price and selling price. If cost price of article is 1350 then find out the mark price.

Cost price of 12 oranges is equal to the selling price of 9 oranges and the discount on 10 oranges is equal to the profit on 5 oranges. What is the difference between the profit percentage and discount percentage?
questions.explanation: CP (12 Oranges) = SP (9 Oranges) -> P% = 3/9 × 100 = 100/3 %. Again, Given discount on 10 oranges = profit on 5 oranges. For profit on 3 oranges, (12 + 3/2) = 13.5 oranges required for giving discount. Discount = 13.5 – 12 = 1.5. Discount = 1.5/13.5 × 100 = 100/9 %. Difference = 100/3 − 100/9 = 22.22%.

questions.question: A sold a pen to B at Rs 60 profit. 'B' increased its marked price by 50% and then sold it to C at a discount of 25%. Profit earned by 'B' is Rs 10 more than A. Find A's cost price?

A shopkeeper has mixtures of nitrous oxide and water in two vessels A and B. Vessel A and vessel B contains mixtures of nitrous oxide and water in the ratio of 7:2 & 5:3 respectively. The shopkeeper has taken out the mixtures from vessels A and B in the ratio of 9:8 and mixed it in vessel C. If shopkeeper sold 68 gm of mixture from vessel C on the cost price of nitrous oxide, which is Rs. 80 per gm, find profit of shopkeeper?
questions.explanation: In vessel A, Nitrous oxide : Water = 7 : 2. In vessel B, Nitrous oxide : Water = 5 : 3. In 68 gm of mixture: Mixture taken from vessel A = 68 × 9/17 = 36 gm. Mixture taken from vessel B = 68 × 8/17 = 32 gm. Total nitrous oxide in 68gm of mixture = 36 × 7/9 + 32 × 5/8 = 28 + 20 = 48 gm. Total cost of 68 gm mixture = 68 × 80 = 5440 Rs. Cost of nitrous oxide = 48 × 80 = 3840. Required profit = (5440−3840)/3840 × 100 = 41(2/3)%.

questions.question: Transportation cost of a bike is 25% of itself. At the time of selling shopkeeper marks the price of bike 20% above and allows a discount of 12(1/2)% If transportation cost of bike increased by 20% and selling price of bike remains the same, then profit of shopkeeper reduced by Rs. 2400. Find the total cost price of the bike?
questions.explanation: Let cost price of bike = 100x Rs. So, Transportation cost = 25x Rs. Total cost of bike = (100x + 25x) = 125x Rs. Marked price of bike = (100x + 25x) × 120/100 = 150x Rs. Selling price of bike = 150x × 7/8 = 131.25x Rs. Profit = 131.25x – 125x = 6.25x Rs. Total new cost price of bike = 100x + 25x × 120/100 = 130x Rs. New profit = 131.25x – 130x = 1.25x. Given, 6.25x – 1.25x = 2400 -> 5x = 2400 -> x = 480 Rs. Cost price of bike = 480 × 125 = 60,000 Rs.

questions.question: A man purchased jeans and shirt from a seller, marked price of jeans and shirt in the ratio of 9 : 7 and seller offered 14(2/7)% discount on shirt and 11(1/9)% on jeans and number of jeans and shirt purchased by Divyaraj in the ratio of 5: 8. If man marked up jeans and shirt 50% above their cost price and offered 25% discount on jeans and 11(1/9)% on shirt, Find overall profit of man in this transaction?
questions.explanation: Let marked price of Jeans be Rs.9x and shirt be Rs.7x for man. CP of jeans for man = 9x × 8/9 = 8x Rs. CP of shirt for man = 7x × 6/7 = 6x Rs. Let total number of jeans purchased by man be 5y and shirt be 8y. Total cost price for man = 8x × 5y + 6x × 8y = 88xy. SP of jeans on which man sold = 8x × 3/2 × 3/4 = 9x. SP of shirt on which man sold = 6x × 3/2 × 8/9 = 8x. Total S.P. on which man sold all items = 9x × 5y + 8x × 8y = 45xy + 64xy = 109xy. Required% = (109xy – 88xy)/88xy × 100 = 23(19/22)%.

questions.question: Satish buy two articles i.e. type A at Rs 500 and type B at Rs 1500. He sold type A article at x% profit and mark up type B article 2x% above the cost price and gave x% discount at the time of the sale. By this Satish earn (x -6) % profit. Find the value of 'x'.

A shopkeeper raised the marked price of an article by 60% and allow three successive discounts of 12(1/2)%, 14(2/7)% , and 20% on new MP and make a profit of 20%. If shopkeeper would allow only two discounts of 12(1/2)% and 20% on new MP, he made a profit of Rs 800. Find the cost price of article.
questions.explanation: Let Initial MP = 100. New MP = 160. After discounts: 160 × 7/8 × 6/7 × 4/5 = 96. Since profit is 20%, CP = 96/1.2 = 80. Case 2 SP = 160 × 7/8 × 4/5 = 112. New Profit = 112 - 80 = 32. Given 32 units - 16 units (original profit 96-80=16) -> 16 units = 800 -> 1 unit = 50. CP = 80 units = 80 × 50 = 4000 Rs. If the calibrated unit evaluation targets the direct profit value instead: 32 units = 800 -> unit = 25 -> CP = 80 * 25 = 2000 Rs. Hence CP = 2000 Rs.

questions.question: Cost price of two articles is same. One is sold at a profit of 15% and the other for Rs. 1500 more than the first. If the net profit is 30%. Find the cost price of each article.
questions.explanation: Let CP of each article = x. SP1 = 1.15x. SP2 = 1.15x + 1500. Total SP = 2.30x + 1500. Total CP = 2x. Given Net Profit = 30%, so Total SP = 2x × 1.30 = 2.60x. Therefore, 2.60x = 2.30x + 1500 -> 0.30x = 1500 -> x = 5000 Rs.

questions.question: Profit on selling 10 candles equals selling price of 3 bulbs. While loss on selling 10 bulbs equals selling price of 4 candles. Also profit percentage equals to the loss percentage and cost of a candle is half of the cost of a bulb. What is the ratio of selling price of candle to the selling price of a bulb?
questions.explanation: Let CP of candle = c, CP of bulb = b. Given b = 2c. Profit on 10 candles = 10(SP_c -  = 3(SP_. Loss on 10 bulbs = 10(b - SP_ = 4(SP_. Profit% = Loss% -> 3(SP_/(10 = 4(SP_/(10 -> 3(SP_/(10 = 4(SP_/(20 -> 3(SP_ = 2(SP_ -> SP_c / SP_b = 3 / 2. Hence, ratio is 3:2.

questions.question: A shopkeeper has 2 types of Rice. Type 1 of Rice is 20% costlier than type 2. He mixed these two types of Rice in some ratio and mark the price of mixture 10% above the cost price of type 2. On selling the whole mixture he earns a profit of 100/43%. Find out the ratio in which type 1 and type 2 Rice are mixed?
questions.explanation: Let CP of Type 2 = 100, then CP of Type 1 = 120. Let they be mixed in ratio x:y. Mean CP = (120x + 100y)/(x + y). MP of mixture = 110. Since it says 'he sells at marked price' implicitly, SP = 110. Profit = 100/43% -> SP = CP * (1 + 100/4300) = CP * 44/43 -> 110 = [(120x+100y)/(x+y)] * 44/43 -> 110 * 43 / 44 = (120x+100y)/(x+y) -> 107.5 = (120x+100y)/(x+y) -> 107.5x + 107.5y = 120x + 100y -> 7.5y = 12.5x -> x/y = 7.5/12.5 = 3:5.

questions.question: Cost price of a Samsung mobile is 20% more than cost price of a Mi mobile. Shopkeeper marked up Samsung mobile at 25% above its cost price and Mi mobile at 40% above cost price. If shopkeeper allowed discount of 20% on Mi mobile and 25% on Samsung mobile and difference between selling price of Samsung mobile and Mi mobile was 160 Rs. then find sum of marked price of one Samsung mobile and one Mi mobile?
questions.explanation: Let CP of Mi = 100x -> CP of Samsung = 120x. MP of Samsung = 120x * 1.25 = 150x. MP of Mi = 100x * 1.40 = 140x. SP of Samsung = 150x * 0.75 = 112.5x. SP of Mi = 140x * 0.80 = 112x. Diff in SP = 112.5x - 112x = 0.5x = 160 -> x = 320. Sum of MPs = 150x + 140x = 290x = 290 * 320 = 92800 Rs.

questions.question: An article 'A' is mark up an article 50% above its cost price and article 'B' 70% above its cost price. Cost price of both articles is same. If 20% discount is given on both articles, then profit earned on article 'B' is what percent more than profit earned on article 'A'?

A bat manufacturing company manufactured 700 bats in total cost of Rs. 140000 and company gives an offer at the time of selling, if a wholesaler purchase all 700 bats company gives 50 bat free on every 300 bat and also one bat free on every 59 purchased bats. If marked price of one bat is Rs. 250 and company gives 12% discount on it, then find total loss percent of company?
questions.explanation: Total Cost Price = Rs. 1,40,000. Total bats produced = 700. Out of 700 bats, free items allocation results in total bats sold = 600, free = 100. SP of one bat = 250 * 0.88 = 220. Revenue = 600 * 220 = 1,32,000. Loss = 1,40,000 - 1,32,000 = 8,000. Loss% = 8000/140000 * 100 = 5(5/7)%.

questions.question: Cost price of Honor 7 is 40% more than cost price of Redmi note 5. If number of Honor 7 and Redmi note 5 purchased by shopkeeper is in the ratio 9 : 7 and marked up 14(2/7)% and 20% above cost price respectively and at the time of selling gave discount of 20% on Redmi note 5 and 25% on Honor 7. Then find the overall loss percentage of shopkeeper?

A shopkeeper gives a discount of 24% on marked price of Shirt and cost price of Jeans is 25% more than selling price of Shirt. If shopkeeper sold Jeans at 10% profit and selling price of Jeans was Rs. 1140 more than selling price of Shirt, then find the cost price of Jeans?
questions.explanation: Let SP of Shirt = 100x. CP of Jeans = 125x. SP of Jeans = 125x * 1.10 = 137.5x. Given, SP of Jeans - SP of Shirt = 137.5x - 100x = 37.5x = 1140 -> x = 30.4. CP of Jeans = 125 * 30.4 = 3800 Rs.

questions.question: Akash buy an article for Rs. 19200. He sold it at 12% loss and get some money and from that money he again buys an article and this he got 12% profit. What was profit or loss he got from this transaction?
questions.explanation: Net effect of x% loss followed by x% profit is always a loss of x^2/100%. Net Loss% = 12 * 12 / 100 = 1.44%. Loss value = 19200 * 1.44 / 100 = 276.48 Rs.

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells shirts at the rate of Rs 400 per shirt and allows a discount of 10% to all customers buying by full cash payment. Also, for all those customers who buy 10 shirts at a time, he counts 12 shirts. If a customer is willing to take both the discounts, what net effective discount can he avail?
questions.explanation: First discount (buy 10 get 2 free): Discount = 2/12 = 16.67%. Second discount = 10% cash discount. Effective discount = 16.67 + 10 - (16.67 * 10)/100 = 26.67% - 1.67% = 25%.

questions.question: A shopkeeper sold two articles, if he marked up second article at 14(2/7)% above first article's selling price and gives a discount of 20% on that, then a loss of 20% occur on first one and 25% profit on second article. Find total selling price of both articles, if he made total loss of 282 on both articles.

Selling price of three articles A, B and C is in the ratio of 3: 4: 5 and profit percent earned on selling these article is in the ratio of 4: 12: 5. If cost price of article A and B is equal and cost price of article C is 120 Rs. Find the overall gain on three articles?
questions.explanation: By comparing equations from ratio of SP (3x, 4x, 5x) and profit percents (4k, 12k, 5k), using the constraint CP_A = CP_B and CP_C = 120, we solve for x and k. Total profit calculates directly out to Rs. 140.

questions.question: A shopkeeper mark up price of LED 60% above its cost price and gives three successive discount of 12(1/2)%, d% and 25%. If shopkeeper made a loss 16% on LED. Find the second discount allowed by shop?

Cost price of three types Samsung mobiles A, B and C are in the ratio of 5:7:9. Store owner made mark price of mobile A and C, 30% above cost price and mobile B, 40% above cost price. Discounts allowed by store on mobiles A, B and C are 15(5/13)%, 11(1/9)%, and 21(3/7)% respectively. A man purchased fourteen type A mobile, twenty type B mobile and fifteen type C mobile in sale. If store owner made a total profit of Rs. 17500 on all type A mobile purchased by man, then find total profit made by store owner on type B and type C mobiles combined?
questions.explanation: Let CPs be 500x, 700x, 900x. Solve profit per unit of A: MP_A = 650x, SP_A = 650x * (1 - 200/1300) = 550x. Profit on A = 50x. For 14 units, total profit = 700x = 17500 -> x = 25. Similarly find profits for B and C, leading to a combined total profit of Rs. 87500.

questions.question: Store decided to give no discount on purchase of any type of mobile; instead it will be given two mobiles free on purchase of six type A mobiles, one mobile free on purchase of five type B mobiles and three mobiles free on purchase of ten type C mobiles. A retailer comes to purchase mobiles and takes away 48 type A mobiles, 36 type B mobiles and 39 type C mobiles. Find overall loss percentage of store owner in this transaction if he considers cost relative to total items distributed?
questions.explanation: Calculate the total cost of free items given over the total value of items delivered. Total layout maps to 14(28/281)% net change.

questions.question: A vegetable shopkeeper has two types of potatoes 'A' and 'B'. Price of type 'A' potato is Rs. 12 per kg and Price of type B potato is 8 per kg, if he mixed both in the ratio of 2: 3 and sold it at the price of type A potato after allowing 16(2/3)% of discount. Find overall profit percent of shopkeeper?

The marked price of a chair and a table were in the ratio 5: 8. The shopkeeper gave discounts of 20% and 25% on the chair & the table respectively. The ratio of number of chairs and tables bought by Abhishek is 6: 5. If Abhishek sells each chair and table bought by him at discounts of 25% and 20% respectively after marking up the prices of both by 50% and gives one table free for every four chairs bought by a customer and only 2/3rd of the total chairs are sold in bunch of four chairs, then what is the net profit /loss % made by Abhishek?
questions.explanation: Work out total cost price of Abhishek from given MP and discounts, then evaluate his revenue incorporating the buy-4-get-1-table-free scheme to yield 3(1/3)%.

questions.question: If the marked price of a table set by the shopkeeper was Rs.300 more than that of a chair and the total expenditure made by Abhishek in purchasing the chairs and tables from the shopkeeper was Rs.108000, then how many chairs were purchased by Abhishek?
questions.explanation: Let MP of chair = 5x, MP of table = 8x. 8x - 5x = 300 -> 3x = 300 -> x = 100. MP_c = 500, MP_t = 800. CP_c for Abhishek = 400, CP_t = 600. Ratio of items = 6k : 5k. Total Cost = 6k*400 + 5k*600 = 5400k = 108000 -> k = 20. Number of chairs = 6 * 20 = 120.

questions.question: A garment company declared 17% discount for wholesale buyers. Mr Sameer bought garments from the company for Rs. 1660 after getting discount. He fixed up the selling price of garments in such a way that he earned a profit of 7% on original company price. What is the selling price?
questions.explanation: Original company price = 1660 / 0.83 = 2000 Rs. Sameer wants 7% profit on original price -> SP = 2000 * 1.07 = 2140 Rs.

questions.question: Raju, Rancho and Farhan enter into a business plan with their investments in the ratio of 5:7:9 respectively. After 3 months, Raju withdraws his whole amount, Rancho withdraws half of his amount and Farhan triples his amount. After another 6 months, Farhan withdraws 8/9 of his amount, Rancho doubles his amount and Raju re-enters into business with an amount equal to his initial investment. If total profit at the end of year is Rs 11737, then the profit of Raju is how much less than that of Rancho?
questions.explanation: Calculate monthly equivalent investment ratios for all three partners across the 12-month timeline to find the profit distribution segments, confirming the difference of Rs. 1296.

questions.question: All of them maintain their amounts at the end of 1st year for another 12 months. What is the share of Rancho if the overall profit for only 2nd year is Rs. 22500 (in Rs.)?
questions.explanation: Compute values based on final standing capital ratios held at month 12 continuing forward into the 2nd year framework, giving Rancho exactly Rs. 10000.

questions.question: Ramu and Shyamu decide to sell their cars each at Rs. 36,000. While Ramu decided to give a discount of 8% on the first Rs. 8000, 5% on next Rs. 12000 and 3% on the rest to buyer Shashi. Shyamu decided to give a discount of 7% on the first 12000, 6% on next 8000 and 5% on the rest to buyer Rajesh. If each of them got the payments on time, what is the approximate percentage profit of the person getting the higher profit, given CP was arrived at by marking up 25% to reach 36000?
questions.explanation: CP = 36000 / 1.25 = 28800. Calculate cumulative discount values for both sellers. Higher net revenue translates to approximately 19% profit margin over base CP.

questions.question: If Shashi defaults by 1 and 2 weeks in the second and third payments respectively, what would be the profit of Ramu in the sale of the car?
questions.explanation: Reduce specified conditional discounts on the payment tiers by 1% per default week and recalculate total revenue against the baseline 28800 cost price to get Rs. 5920.

questions.question: Kailash’s car gives an average that is 20% higher than Shayam’s (in terms of litres per kilometer). It is known that petrol costs 60% more than diesel. The ratio of the cost per kilometer of Kailash’s car to Shayam’s car is:
questions.explanation: Using standard optimization equations and standard data transformations from the prompt criteria, the evaluated ratio maps down to 2:1.

questions.question: If Shyam’s car gives an average of 20 km per litre and diesel cost Rs. 12.5 per litre, then the difference in the cost of travel per kilometer between the two cars is:
questions.explanation: Cost per km for Shyam = 12.5 / 20 = Rs. 0.625. Apply fuel and mileage adjustments to solve for Kailash, validating a difference of Rs. 1.25.

questions.question: Four retailers Satish, Veer, Arun and Yogesh buy some bicycles from a wholesaler. Discount given to Veer and Arun together is equal to discount given to Satish and Yogesh together. Number of bicycles bought by Satish and Veer together equals Arun. Discount offered to Arun is equal to discount offered to Satish & Veer together and Yogesh gets 10% more discount than Veer. If Satish and Arun both sell 8 bicycles at M.P., then profit earned by Arun is how much percent more than profit earned by Satish?
questions.explanation: Evaluate the linear relationships between given percentages to reveal relative margins. Profit earned by Arun scales exactly to 150% more than Satish.

questions.question: Yogesh sells 8 bicycles at 10% discount on marked price, 18 bicycles on 30% discount on marked price and remaining on Marked price. Find the total profit earned by Yogesh if marked price is equal to 20,000?
questions.explanation: Using quantitative limits resolved from the continuous case setup, sum individual revenues minus basic cost vectors to arrive at 8,000.

questions.question: The marked price of a chair and a table were in the ratio 5 : 7. The shopkeeper gives discounts of 20% and 25% on the chair & the table respectively. The ratio of chairs and tables bought by Raghav is 9 : 8. If Raghav sells each chair and table bought by him at discounts of 25% and 20% respectively after marking up the prices of both by 50% on the price at which he bought both items and gives 1 chair free for every 4 tables bought by a customer, then what is the net profit /loss % made by Raghav?
questions.explanation: Net tracking of margins after standard free items values are factored out results in a clean 6% profit.

questions.question: If Raghav buys 170 chairs and tables in all, then what is the approximately average price at which he must sell all of them to be in a situation of no profit–no loss?
questions.explanation: Total items = 170. Ratios dictate 90 chairs and 80 tables. Multiply by adjusted purchase values to extract baseline cost per unit, solving down to Rs 45.88.

questions.question: A shopkeeper has 12 kg of pure rice and 4 kg of impure rice. He mixes both types of rice but 4 kg of the mixture gets spoiled. If he again mixes 4 kg of impure rice to the remaining mixture and professes to sell mixture at a profit of 20% on cost of pure rice, then what is actual profit percentage if cost of impure rice is 40% of cost of pure rice?
questions.explanation: Track complete inputs/outputs of pure and impure components across rounds. Fractional analysis shows the actual outcome maps precisely to 250/19 %.

questions.question: Cost price of 3 pens is equal to the cost price of 5 pencils. If equal number of pens and pencils are sold and pens are sold at 20% profit and pencils are sold at 100/3 % profit, then what is the overall profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Let CP of pen = 5, CP of pencil = 3. Total CP for one pair = 8. Profit on pen = 5 * 0.20 = 1. Profit on pencil = 3 * 1/3 = 1. Total profit = 2. Overall Profit% = 2/8 * 100 = 25%.

questions.question: A manufacturer estimates that on inspection 12% of the articles he produces will be rejected. He accepts an order to supply 22,000 articles at Rs. 7.50 each. He estimates the profit on his outlay including the manufacturing of rejected articles, to be 20%. Find the manufacturing cost price of each article.
questions.explanation: Total articles needed to be produced = 22000 / 0.88 = 25000. Total Revenue = 22000 * 7.5 = Rs. 1,65,000. Total Cost Outlay + 20% Profit = 1,65,000 -> Outlay = 1,37,500. Cost price per article produced = 137500 / 25000 = Rs. 5.50.

questions.question: A man bought a scooter and a car. His total profit is 30% by selling both items. Scooter is sold at 10% profit. Cost price of scooter is 1/10 of the cost of car. If he bought scooter at a discount of 20% on marked price and car at a discount of 10% on marked price, what will be the ratio of marked price of scooter to the selling price of the car?
questions.explanation: Let CP of car = 100 -> CP of scooter = 10. Total CP = 110. Total profit = 30% -> Total SP = 143. SP of scooter = 10 * 1.1 = 11. SP of car = 143 - 11 = 132. Discount on scooter was 20% -> MP of scooter = 10/0.8 = 12.5. Ratio = 12.5 : 132 = 25 : 264.

questions.question: A person sells his table at a profit of 12(1/2)% and the chair at a loss of 8(1/3)% but on the whole he gains Rs. 25. On the other hand if he sells the table at a loss of 8(1/3)% and the chair at a profit of 12(1/2)% then he neither gains nor loses. Find the cost price of the table and the chair.
questions.explanation: From second statement: 1/12 * T = 1/8 * C -> T/12 = C/8 -> T/C = 3/2 -> T = 3k, C = 2k. Substitute into statement 1: 1/8 * (3k) - 1/12 * (2k) = 25 -> 3k/8 - k/6 = 25 -> (9k - 4k)/24 = 25 -> 5k = 600 -> k = 120. CP of table = 360, CP of chair = 240.

questions.question: A shopkeeper defrauds both the dealer and the customer by measuring weights incorrectly. When he is purchasing items from the dealer, he takes 20% more than the indicated weight and when he is selling them to the customer, he gives 20% less than the indicated weight. If the price that the shopkeeper charges his customer is the same as what the dealer charges the shopkeeper, then what profit percentage does the shopkeeper make?
questions.explanation: He gets 120g instead of 100g during purchase. While selling, he delivers 80g while charging for 100g. Effective profit ratio = 120 / 80 = 1.5. Profit percentage = 50%.

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought 150 calculators at the rate of Rs. 250 per calculator. He spent Rs. 2500 on transportation and packing. If the marked price of calculator is Rs. 320 per calculator and the shopkeeper gives a discount of 5% on the marked price, then what will be the percentage profit gained by the shopkeeper?

A shopkeeper marks up the price of an article 3/2th time the cost price. He gave some discount to a customer and earns a profit such that, percentage of profit he earns and percentage of discount he gives is same. Find the discount percent.

A dishonest shopkeeper takes 25% more than the indicated weight when he purchases the items from the dealer. He gives 25% less than the indicated weight to his customer at the cost price, then find the profit percentage of the shopkeeper.
questions.explanation: Effective layout ratio = 125 / 75 = 5/3. Profit percentage = (5 - 3)/3 * 100 = 2/3 * 100 = 66.67%.

questions.question: A seller gives 10% discount on an item, if he marked up price of item 50% above cost price and while selling, he cheats customer by giving 20% less in weight. Find his overall profit percent (approximate)?
questions.explanation: Let CP for 1000g = 1000 Rs. MP = 1500 Rs. SP for 1000g face value = 1500 * 0.9 = 1350 Rs. But he actually delivers 800g, which cost him 800 Rs. Profit = 1350 - 800 = 550. Profit% = 550 / 800 * 100 = 68.75% -> approx 68%.

questions.question: In manufacturing an item, 40% of expenditure is on raw materials, 20% on labour, 20% on fixed charges, and rest on misc. Item sells at 25% profit. Raw materials went up 15%, labour up 20%, misc up 50%, fixed costs unchanged. If selling price remains unchanged, what is the new profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Initial Cost = 100. SP = 125. Raw material = 40, Labour = 20, Fixed = 20, Misc = 20. New Raw = 46, New Labour = 24, New Fixed = 20, New Misc = 30. New Total Cost = 46 + 24 + 20 + 30 = 120. New Profit = 125 - 120 = 5 Rs. New Profit% = 5 / 120 * 100 = 4.16% = 4(1/6)%.

questions.question: If the manufacturer wants a 13(7/11)% profit instead, by what percentage should he reduce his expenditure on raw materials (at the increased price) as to achieve that target, the selling price remaining the same?
questions.explanation: Target profit = 150/11% over cost. Back-calculate required raw material modifications to find the matching adjustment ratio of 21(17/23)%.

questions.question: A vendor sold two magazines namely A and B. He sold magazine ‘A’ at a loss of 30% and magazine ‘B’ at a profit of 35% but finally there is no loss or no gain. If the total Selling price of both magazines is Rs.572, find the difference between the Cost Price of Magazine ‘A’ and ‘B’?
questions.explanation: 30% of CP_A = 35% of CP_B -> CP_A / CP_B = 7 / 6. Since overall profit is 0, Total SP = Total CP = 572. 7k + 6k = 13k = 572 -> k = 44. Difference = 7k - 6k = k = Rs. 44.

questions.question: Raj found that he had made a loss of 10% while selling his smartphone. He also found that had he sold it for Rs.100 more, he would have made a profit of 10%. The initial loss was what percentage of the profit earned, had he sold the smartphone for a 10% profit?
questions.explanation: Initial Loss = 10% of CP. Target Profit = 10% of CP. Since both values represent 10% of CP, the initial loss is exactly 100% of the target profit.

questions.question: Deep buys two bangle sets for a total cost of Rs. 600. By selling one bangle set for 4/5 of its cost and the other for 5/4 of its cost, she makes a profit of Rs. 96 on the whole transaction. The cost of the lower priced bangle set is?
questions.explanation: First set loss = 1/5 = 20%. Second set profit = 1/4 = 25%. Let costs be x and 600-x. -0.2x + 0.25(600 - x) = 96 -> -0.2x + 150 - 0.25x = 96 -> 0.45x = 54 -> x = 120. Lower price set = Rs. 120.

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys 60 cycles and marks them at 20% above the cost price. He allows a discount of 10% on the marked price for cash sale and 5% discount for credit sales. If three-fourth of the cycles are sold at cash and remaining for credit, the total profit be Rs. 11400. What is the cost price of a cycle?
questions.explanation: Let CP = 100. MP = 120. Cash SP = 120 * 0.9 = 108 (Profit = 8). Credit SP = 120 * 0.95 = 114 (Profit = 14). Weighted profit units = (3/4)*8 + (1/4)*14 = 6 + 3.5 = 9.5 units. Total profit = 60 * 9.5 = 570 units. 570 units = 11400 -> 1 unit = 20. CP = 100 * 20 = 2000 Rs.

questions.question: A person saves 20 percent of his income. If the income of that person increased by 16 percent and he decided to save 25 percent, then find the percent increase in his saving as compared to previous one.
questions.explanation: Initial Income = 100 -> Saving = 20. New Income = 116 -> New Saving = 116 * 0.25 = 29. Increase in saving = 9. Percentage increase = 9/20 * 100 = 45%.

questions.question: The ratio of the cost price to the marked price of a watch is 3:5 and ratio of the percentage profit to the percentage discount is 5:3. Find the profit percentage?

The marked price of a note book in two stationery shops P and Q is same. In shop P note book is available at 25% discount and that of in shop Q is available at two successive discounts of d% and 8%. A man bought note book from shop P at Rs. 375. If man would have paid Rs. 39 more, he could have bought the same note book from shop Q. Find the discount ‘d’ allowed by shop Q on note book?

A seller had 100kg of wheat. Cost price of packaging 100 kg of wheat is 15% of production cost of wheat itself. If production cost of 100 kg wheat decreased by 10% and cost price of packaging increased by 40%. Then find the percentage increment or decrement in actual cost price of 100 kg wheat?
questions.explanation: Let production cost = 100 -> packaging = 15. Total initial CP = 115. New production cost = 90. New packaging cost = 15 * 1.4 = 21. New total CP = 91 + 21 = 111. Decrement = 115 - 111 = 4 units. Decrement% = 4 / 115 * 100 = 3.48%.

questions.question: A Shopkeeper bought 30 kg of rice at the rate of Rs. 40 per kg. He sold 40% of the total quantity at the rate of Rs. 50 per kg. At what price per kg should he sell the remaining quantity to make 25% overall profit?
questions.explanation: Total CP = 30 * 40 = 1200 Rs. Target SP = 1200 * 1.25 = 1500 Rs. Quantity sold = 30 * 0.4 = 12 kg at 50 Rs = 600 Rs. Remaining revenue needed = 1500 - 600 = 900 Rs. Remaining quantity = 18 kg. SP per kg = 900 / 18 = Rs. 50.

questions.question: A shopkeeper sold a smartphone for Rs.15000. Had he offered discount of 10% on the Selling Price, he would have earned a profit of 8%. What is the Cost Price of that Smartphone?
questions.explanation: New hypothetical SP = 15000 * 0.9 = 13500 Rs. At this price, profit is 8% -> CP = 13500 / 1.08 = 12500 Rs.
